column3: Knowledge that has arrived establishes a direct contrast to remaining without guidance.
Being left without divine support gives a broad counterpart to the focus's abandonment.
It directly joins the arrival of a clear messenger with failure of remembrance.
It identifies Satan as the force that provokes rupture between people and as humanity's open enemy.
The same surah directly links forgetting the remembrance to ruin after prolonged ease.
The human question about the shaken earth does not clarify misguidance after remembrance.
Satan's declared enmity to humanity supplies a related warning, though the setting is different.
The immediately preceding regret over taking a close companion supplies the focus's human agent.
Satanic whispering shows a mechanism of diversion, but not abandonment after the reminder arrives.
It closely parallels Satan's sequence of urging wrongdoing and then disowning the person.
The immediate continuation names the outcome as the community's abandonment of the Quran.
It defines the revealed remembrance as something explained so that people may reflect.
Human wishing does not add to the focus's account of diverted remembrance.
The devils' exclusion from hearing is only a remote contrast to their role in misguidance.
A reminder and warner having come before belated regret supports the focus's post-arrival setting.
It directly depicts people disputing whether influential others diverted them after guidance came.
The same surah presents repeated signs as an occasion for remembrance that most refuse.
The resulting state of being forsaken gives a close consequence parallel to Satan's abandonment.
Its use of remembrance as prior scripture is distinct from the focus's reception and loss of it.
The mention of Moses receiving the Book only broadly supports the chapter's prophetic context.
Calling an account a remembrance does not clarify being turned away from revelation.
Human striving does not address the focus's misleading companion or remembrance.
The same-surah description of being more astray in way develops the focus's path outcome.
The exclusion of devils as revelation's source contrasts with their role in turning people from it.
The gendered rhetorical question does not clarify the focus.
Continuing blindness and greater path-loss is a broad consequence parallel already covered locally.
Human labor toward the Lord does not explain diversion from remembrance.
The creation formula does not clarify the focus.
The alternation of night and day is explicitly made for those who seek remembrance or gratitude.
The command to remind supports the active communicative role of remembrance, though it is less specific.
Seeking protection from Satan is a general preventative response rather than the focus's completed misguidance.
The chapter's enemies of every prophet extend the focus's hostile social setting.
Seeking refuge when Satan provokes gives a direct corrective to the focus's satanic pressure.
Clear proofs having come before a commanded change of allegiance parallels revelation received and acted upon.
Seeing a destroyed town without expecting resurrection only broadly reflects refusal to learn from evidence.
Calling manifest truth magic when it arrives closely parallels rejection after disclosure.
Satanic incitement causing estrangement between brothers offers a related interpersonal mechanism.
The question about former generations does not clarify the focus.
Turning away from God's remembrance and preferring worldly life directly develops the focus's loss of it.
It names the Quran as possessing remembrance, clarifying the object from which the focus is diverted.
The nearby objection to a human messenger supplies background but not the focus's companion mechanism.
The arrival of promised punishment is a remote aftermath of rejecting what came.
It prohibits obeying one whose heart is heedless of remembrance and follows desire, closely matching harmful influence.
The difficult judgment day is a local consequence but adds little to the causal account.
It directly warns that Satan can bar people from the way as their open enemy.
Messengers remove excuse after arrival, reinforcing the accountability presupposed by the focus.
The local accusation sequence ends in the opponents' loss of the way.
Seeking refuge from satanic promptings supplies a practical countermeasure to their pressure.
Remembering divine aid is a general positive use of remembrance, not the focus's departure from it.
The destruction of deniers in the surrounding historical examples is only an indirect consequence.
It states Satan's enmity, summons, and intended destination, extending the focus's characterization of him.
Turning away after rescue illustrates human ingratitude, but not satanic diversion from remembrance.
Those led admit that obedience to social superiors caused their loss of the way.
It shows earlier peoples denying messengers despite clear proofs and illuminated scripture arriving.
Following desire despite knowledge and then failing to remember gives a related inner mechanism of misguidance.
The local distinction between misleading others and losing the way oneself sharpens responsibility in the focus.
It explicitly joins guidance with remembrance, clarifying what is lost when one is diverted from it.
Inherited error supplies a broad social pattern for accepting a misleading way.
The punishment of Noah's people is a local warning but adds little beyond the earlier consequence cards.
It identifies the revealed remembrance as divinely sent down and preserved.
The hidden protection of an orphan's treasure does not clarify the focus.
The lack of any protector or helper is a distant counterpart to being forsaken.
It excludes Satan as the source of the Quran, providing a useful boundary to his corrupting role.
The believers' pledge and divine approval do not clarify the focus.
The humanity of earlier messengers is nearby context but does not add to diverted remembrance.
The creator contrast and call to remember are too general for the focus.
The messenger recites, purifies, and teaches the Book after prior manifest error, directly reversing the focus's condition.
God neither errs nor forgets, but this does not address human abandonment of remembrance.
Becoming an ally of Satan presents the inverse of taking the messenger's way.
Material provision and gratitude do not add a close link after the stronger remembrance evidence.
The immediately preceding wish to have taken a path with the messenger supplies the positive alternative.
The person coming eagerly does not clarify the focus.
False associates disappear and claimed ties are severed, giving a judgment counterpart to abandonment.
The bare statement of a sign adds no specific link.
Sudden punishment of towns is only a general consequence of error.
Satan's own disobedience to the Merciful grounds the warning against serving him.
The same opponents portray the messenger as leading them away from their gods, directly continuing the local reversal.
Devils driving disbelievers shows their active inciting role, though without the remembrance wording.
Association with devils through wastefulness is a separate ethical setting.
God taking Abraham as a close friend supplies only a distant contrast to the harmful companion.
Following every rebellious Satan without knowledge gives a direct pattern of misguided allegiance.
Preferring worldly good until it distracts from remembrance directly illustrates the focus's displacement of it.
The chapter intensifies its verdict through failure to hear or reason and greater path-loss.
Refusing to remember when reminded directly parallels the focus's broken reception of remembrance.
The primordial command not to worship Satan names him as humanity's open enemy and specifies the required refusal.
No protecting allies and no path after misguidance develops the forsaken result.
It identifies concrete practices as Satan's work and commands avoidance, supplying an applied form of resistance.
Establishing prayer for God's remembrance provides a positive practice opposed to being turned from it.
The same surah presents freely taking a way to the Lord as the alternative to the focus's regret.
The generic appeal to remember adds little after the fuller remembrance passages.
The rhetorical question about judgment does not clarify the focus.
Failure to reflect on the message and treating it as unprecedented supports a reception failure after speech arrives.
The limited human knowledge of the spirit does not clarify the focus.
Guidance has come, yet people reject it because the messenger is human, closely paralleling post-arrival refusal.
Teaching expression does not clarify diverted remembrance.
Resenting being reminded rather than responding to the warning gives a direct rejection pattern.
The opportunist's envy of others' success does not clarify the focus.
The raising of the messenger's mention does not address turning from the remembrance.
Manifest error is named generally, without the focus's causal relation to a companion or Satan.
Satanic forgetting of the reminder and the command to leave wrongful company closely combines both focus mechanisms.
Satan declares that he only invited people, then disowns them after their response, making the focus's forsaking explicit.
Turning from the Merciful's remembrance results in an attached satanic companion, directly joining remembrance and companionship.
Those satanic companions divert people from the way while they suppose themselves guided, extending the focus's deception.
Satan seeks to create enmity and bar people from God's remembrance and prayer, directly naming his obstructing work.
Satan makes his party forget God's remembrance, closely paralleling the focus's turning away from it.
It calls Satan an evil companion, providing a direct boundary against the focus's harmful close relationship.
Satan declares his intention to sit on God's straight path after his own deviation and obstruct people.
Satan's approach from every direction describes the sustained pressure behind human ingratitude and diversion.
Satan vows to make wrongdoing attractive and lead people astray, supplying a stated mechanism for the focus's misguidance.
Satan is permitted to incite, mobilize, and make promises, while his promises are declared deceptive.
Taking Satan and his progeny as protecting allies instead of God gives a direct counterpart to the disastrous friendship in the focus.
Taking one's desire as a god gives an inner rival to the remembrance from which the focus's speaker was diverted.
Satan's having led many people astray makes his broad human effect explicit.
After guidance becomes clear, Satan entices and promises people, closely matching post-arrival reversal.
Forgetting God results in forgetting oneself, giving a severe reciprocal consequence of abandoning remembrance.
Satan promises poverty and commands indecency, illustrating how his inducements redirect judgment and conduct.
Satan makes people slip because of what they had earned, offering a related account of moral deflection.
Satan intends to lead those seeking false judgment far astray despite their claim to belief.
Following Satan rather than God begins a compact account of destructive misplaced allegiance.
Satan's promises and wishful hopes are explicitly called deception, clarifying the credibility of his invitation.
Satan makes deeds seem fair, a recurrent mechanism for persisting after signs and warnings.
Being called back to error after God has guided gives a close reversal pattern to the focus.
The person who casts off signs and is followed by Satan supplies a sign-rejection counterpart.
Those touched by Satan remember and then see clearly, providing the focus's possible corrective reversal.
Satan adorns conduct and then withdraws from his allies at confrontation, paralleling his abandonment.
Satan causes forgetfulness of remembrance of the Lord, retaining the focus's key causal language in another setting.
Satan's beautifying of former peoples' deeds explains how misguidance can persist after warning.
Seeking refuge in God before recitation provides a direct preventative practice against satanic interference with remembrance.
Satan lacks authority over God's servants, setting a boundary to the power implied by the focus's experience.
Satan's whisper to Adam offers an early case of deceptive promise leading away from command.
Following divine guidance is explicitly contrasted with going astray or suffering, naming the positive path absent in the focus.
Satan attempts interference with communicated revelation, while God removes it, giving a broader revelation-side contrast.
Following Satan's steps leads to indecency and wrong, framing diversion as an accumulative course.
Satan makes a people's deeds fair and bars them from the way, closely matching the focus's path language.
Satan beautifies deeds and diverts people from the way despite their capacity to perceive.
Following inherited practice is contrasted with Satan's call toward punishment, adding a social pathway of harmful obedience.
Most people follow Iblis except a believing group, supplying a broad pattern of satanic following.
Beautifully presented evil can be seen as good, explaining how a person may embrace a diverted course.
Evil companions beautify present and past conduct, supplying a human-social analogue to the focus's harmful companion.
Wealth and children can distract from God's remembrance, identifying a non-personal route into the focus's loss.
The retreating whisperer provides the Quran's concise portrait of recurrent hidden satanic prompting.
Its whispering into human hearts identifies the interior site at which diversion can begin.
